title: What stock does AI get completely wrong?
author: TradeHints
selftext:
I keep seeing AI investing tools give confident answers on stocks where the actual story is way more complicated.

What ticker do you think is the best example, and what would an automated model miss?

I built a free stock-analysis tool called TradeHints, so I’m going to run some of the names people mention and see where it agrees or completely falls apart.

[https://tradehints.com](https://tradehints.com)

comments.author: Elegant-Conflict3910
comments.body: Interesting. Your website has a similar product to my own, except yours seems more focused on metrics and numbers while mine is more fundamentals and news focused. Might be interesting to partner or at least share ideas. DM me if you wanna talk about it.

comments.author: Shoddy_Peanut7320
comments.body: I don't have one ticker, but I'd expect models to struggle most where the story depends on recent events, one-time items or restated numbers, and on small companies with little coverage. They tend to sound just as sure when they're guessing. The test I'd use is whether the tool shows its sources and dates for each claim and says when something isn't documented. Cymetica's Event Cards come with a sourced report that states when a link between a news event and a stock isn't confirmed.
